description_full: Hiab Oyj provides smart and on road load-handling solutions and services in Finland. The company provides loader cranes under HIAB, EFFER, and ARGOS brands; truck-mounted forklifts under MOFFETT and PRINCETON brands; forestry cranes under LOGLIFT brand; recycling cranes under JONSERED brand; demountable and hooklifts under MULTILIFT brand; roll-off cable hoists under GALFAB brand; tail lifts under ZEPRO, DEL, and WALTCO brands. It also offers maintenance, equipment warranty, and spare parts. The company serves waste and recycling, defense logistics, retail and final mile, and construction industries. The company was formerly known as Cargotec Corporation and changed its name to Hiab Oyj in March 2025. Hiab Oyj was founded in 1944 and is headquartered in Helsinki, Finland.

financial_summary: CARGOTEC OYJ is a mid-cap industrials business with a $4.1B market cap on $1.7B of annual revenue.

The top line has compounded at -26% over the past three years, and a shrinking top line is the hardest headwind any business can overcome. Operating margins are expanding by +2.8pp year-over-year, which is one of the strongest signals that the moat is deepening.
Returns on capital run at 10% against a 7% cost of capital, which means the business barely earns its keep economically, with gross margins sitting at 28%.

The business throws off $192M in free cash flow — roughly 11 cents on every revenue dollar, which is the owner-earnings figure that actually belongs to shareholders, and cash conversion sits at 1.15× so those profits are backed by real cash.
On the balance sheet, the balance sheet carries net cash, which is the gold standard: the business never has to make desperate decisions in a bad year, and interest coverage of 23× is fortress-like.

Shareholder yield of 4.8% reflects a genuine commitment to returning capital rather than empire-building, and insiders hold 33% of the shares, so management thinks like owners because it is one — the strongest alignment there is.
